Serum is the clear liquid that remains after blood has clotted.
During clotting, fibrinogen and other clotting proteins are converted into the clot or trapped within it, so they are removed from the fluid.
After clotting, centrifugation separates the clot and cells from this fluid, leaving the protein‑depleted liquid.
Answer: Serum

Correct answer: Plastid
Plastids are membrane-bound organelles in plant cells, including chloroplasts, chromoplasts and leucoplasts.
They perform plant-specific roles such as photosynthesis, pigment synthesis and storage.
These structures and functions are absent from higher animal cells, so plastid is the organelle unique to plants.

records.explanation:
Answer: Malpighian tubules
They are slender, blind-ended tubes in insects that remove nitrogenous wastes and help regulate water and ions.
They open into the gut at the midgut–hindgut junction so wastes are deposited into the alimentary canal for elimination.
This anatomy and function make Malpighian tubules the insect structures responsible for metabolic waste removal.

records.explanation:
Height is a continuous trait because people show a smooth range of values rather than distinct categories.
Many genes (polygenic inheritance) each contribute small effects to height, producing intermediate phenotypes.
Environmental factors (e.g. nutrition and health) further shift individuals' stature, blurring discrete classes into a continuum.
Answer: Height

records.sourceLabel: Owner-provided Biology non-diagram collection — pending provenance review
records.explanation:
Photosynthesis removes CO2 from the atmosphere by fixing it into organic molecules.
Plants, algae and cyanobacteria use light energy to convert atmospheric CO2 into carbohydrates.
That carbon is stored in plant biomass or transferred to consumers, making photosynthesis the main short-term atmospheric carbon sink.
Correct answer: Photosynthesis

records.sourceLabel: Owner-provided Biology non-diagram collection — pending provenance review
records.explanation:
Amoeba ingests food by extending parts of its cytoplasm called pseudopodia.
Pseudopodia form by cytoplasmic streaming and actin-mediated extension of the cell surface.
They surround and enclose food particles to form a food vacuole where digestion occurs (phagocytosis).
Pseudopodia

records.explanation:
Cervical vertebrae have characteristic transverse foramina located in their transverse processes.
Those foramina form a protected channel through which the vertebral arteries ascend toward the skull.
In most people the vertebral artery passes through the transverse foramina from C6 up to C1 before entering the cranial cavity via the foramen magnum.
Correct answer: Cervical vertebrae

records.explanation:
African Trypanosomiasis
It is caused by the protozoan Trypanosoma brucei which infects humans.
Transmission occurs when an infected tsetse fly (Glossina) bites a person and introduces the parasite into the bloodstream.
Because the disease is specifically spread by tsetse fly bites, African Trypanosomiasis is the correct answer.

records.explanation:
Apoplast pathway
It moves water through porous cell walls and the spaces between cells (the apoplast) rather than through cell interiors.
Because water stays in the cell wall matrix and extracellular spaces, it does not cross plasma membranes or enter the cytoplasm.
This direct flow through cell walls explains why the apoplast pathway matches the question's condition of movement without crossing cell membranes.

records.explanation:
The iris is a pigmented muscular diaphragm surrounding the pupil.
Its muscles change pupil diameter to regulate the amount of light entering the eye.
Sphincter pupillae (constricts) and dilator pupillae (dilates) adjust pupil size under different light levels.
Answer: Iris

records.sourceLabel: Owner-provided Biology non-diagram collection — pending provenance review
records.explanation:
Spirogyra is a filamentous green alga with chlorophyll arranged in spiral chloroplasts.
Those chloroplasts capture light and perform photosynthesis inside each cell.
Photosynthesis converts carbon dioxide and water into organic compounds used for growth and energy.
Correct answer: Autotrophic

records.sourceLabel: Owner-provided Biology non-diagram collection — pending provenance review
records.explanation:
Photolysis is the light-driven splitting of water into protons (H+), electrons and molecular oxygen during the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis.
When chlorophyll absorbs photons it becomes excited and loses electrons; those lost electrons are replaced by electrons released from the photolysis of water.
The electrons and protons produced by photolysis enter the electron transport chain and are used to generate ATP and reduce NADP+ to NADPH.
Answer: Photolysis

records.explanation:
Huntington's disease
It is autosomal dominant, so a single copy of the mutant allele is sufficient to cause the disorder.
The mutation is an expanded CAG repeat in the HTT gene that leads to progressive neurodegeneration when present in one allele.
Because heterozygotes show symptoms with only one mutant allele, Huntington's disease is the correct choice.

records.sourceLabel: Owner-provided Biology non-diagram collection — pending provenance review
records.explanation:
A legume is a dry, dehiscent fruit that develops from a single carpel.
At maturity it characteristically splits open along both dorsal and ventral sutures.
Those two sutures open to release the seeds, which is the defining feature of a legume.
Correct answer: Legume

records.sourceLabel: Owner-provided Biology non-diagram collection — pending provenance review
records.explanation:
Xylem is the vascular tissue that conducts water and dissolved mineral salts from the roots to the aerial parts of the plant.
Its conducting elements, vessels and tracheids, are lignified and connect end-to-end to form continuous tubes.
These tubes allow upward movement of water driven by transpiration pull and the cohesion-tension mechanism.
Xylem

records.sourceLabel: Owner-provided Biology non-diagram collection — pending provenance review
records.explanation:
Mitochondrion
It is the organelle where most cellular respiration occurs and where the bulk of ATP is produced.
Its double membrane and inner folds (cristae) contain the enzymes for the Krebs cycle and the electron transport chain, enabling oxidative phosphorylation.
Mitochondria also have their own DNA and ribosomes to make proteins required for those respiratory functions.

records.sourceLabel: Owner-provided Biology non-diagram collection — pending provenance review
records.explanation:
Transpiration is the loss of water vapor from leaf surfaces through stomata driven by the vapor pressure difference between moist internal air and the outside air.
High humidity raises the moisture level outside the leaf, so the external vapor pressure becomes closer to the internal vapor pressure.
This smaller vapor pressure gradient reduces diffusion of water vapor out of the leaf, so less water is lost.
High humidity

records.sourceLabel: Owner-provided Biology non-diagram collection — pending provenance review
records.explanation:
Marginal placentation means the ovules are attached along the single ventral suture of one carpel.
Legumes have a unicarpellary ovary, so their ovules are borne on that ventral margin.
Because of this attachment the ovules line up in a single row along the seam where the carpel edges meet.
Marginal

records.sourceLabel: Owner-provided Biology non-diagram collection — pending provenance review
records.explanation:
Nephron is the structural and functional unit of the kidney.
Filtration occurs in the renal corpuscle — the glomerulus plus Bowman's capsule — where blood plasma is first filtered into the nephron tubule.
Blood reaches the glomerulus via an afferent arteriole and hydrostatic pressure drives water and small solutes across capillary walls into Bowman's capsule as filtrate.
Because this blood filtration occurs within the renal corpuscle of each nephron, Nephron is the correct answer.

records.explanation:
Jean-Baptiste Lamarck propounded the "use and disuse" theory.
He proposed that organs become more developed with frequent use and diminish or disappear with disuse.
He taught that such acquired changes are passed to offspring, which he presented as a mechanism for evolutionary change.
Jean-Baptiste Lamarck
